gates.decides: Whether a Stryker run passes: which mutants count as detected, which survivors an allowance covers, and when an allowance is stale or ambiguous
gates.impact: A surviving mutant, a stale allowance or an unevaluated mutant passes silently and every project using test-gates loses its real guard

gates.decides: Per-file line coverage from an lcov tracefile and whether each gate is at 100%
gates.impact: A gate with uncovered lines, or with no record at all, passes

gates.decides: Whether a negative control held: the gate failed, and failed on the threshold of the file whose spec was left out
gates.impact: A gate that measures nothing is reported as working

gates.decides: Whether test-gates.json and each allowance in it are well formed (reason required, no duplicates, no path in both lists)
gates.impact: An allowance without a reason or a duplicated gate is accepted, and configs are derived from a broken list

gates.decides: Where the spec of a gate lives, and whether a path is itself a spec
gates.impact: The gate run and the negative control look at the wrong spec, or a missing spec is not noticed

gates.decides: Which command-line arguments belong to test-gates and which are handed to Stryker
gates.impact: An argument meant for Stryker reaches the judge or is dropped, and a typo in an option is silently ignored

expectedTimeouts.reason: With an empty body the loop index never advances, so parseArgs never returns for any non-empty command line
After an option with a separate value the parser would return to the option itself and read it again forever

gates.decides: Allowlist mode: which package imports and which project imports a gate may have, and which gates import another gate
gates.impact: A gate imports an SDK or a service file unnoticed and stops being a pure module

gates.decides: Whether a Vitest setup can report 100% branches with the skipped side of an if untested
gates.impact: A project keeps a coverage floor that has a hole in it without being told

candidates.decides: The static rules for a gate and its spec (decorators, impure imports, ignore directives, skipped tests, self-mocks)
candidates.blocker: Its spec holds the forbidden patterns (it.skip, ignore directives) as test data, which the spec rules reject; move that data out of the spec file. Whitespace-quantifier mutants of the regular expressions also survive

candidates.decides: Which modules a source file imports at runtime
candidates.blocker: About twenty mutants of the regular expressions survive (whitespace quantifiers, sort order of the result). Needs tests per quantifier or a tokenizer instead of regular expressions

The default tables are data: mutants of their reason strings survive, and the specs call resolveSettings while being collected, which makes most mutants static. Split the tables from the validation first
